faqs.q: How do I find my textbook?
faqs.a: Ordering items is done through School Locker: select 'Subjects', choose your semester, search by unit code, then add items to your cart and check out. Wimmera-based students can also purchase from the Horsham Campus Bookshop (phone 5362 2651 or email horsham.bookshop@federation.edu.au).

eMIMSelite is the web version of MIMS — Australia's comprehensive pharmaceutical database, covering over 4,500 prescription and non-prescription drugs. Federation University students and staff can log in using their university credentials.

faqs.q: How long can I borrow books for?
faqs.a: It depends on your student type: Undergraduate and TAFE students can borrow books for 14 days (2 weeks), and Postgraduate students can borrow for 42 days (6 weeks). Textbooks are a 2-week loan for all Fed Uni staff and students.

Hours vary by campus and change regularly — Mt Helen, Gippsland and Berwick are typically 8:30am-5pm, SMB is 8:30am-4:30pm, and Wimmera is 10am-2pm on weekdays. Always check the Library's live hours page for today's exact hours, since they can vary.

faqs.q: How do I contact the library?
faqs.a: You can chat with a librarian online, email library@federation.edu.au, call 1800 333 864 (1800 FED UNI), or visit any of our five campus libraries. Live support is generally available 9am-5pm Monday to Friday.

faqs.q: How do I book a study space?
faqs.a: You can reserve a meeting room or study space in advance through the Library's online booking system, so you've got a space when you need it.

faqs.q: What quicklinks do current students need?
faqs.a: The main student systems are my Student Centre, Moodle, student email (Outlook), mySchedule, the Co-op placement portal, and InPlace — all accessible from the Current Students page.

faqs.q: Who do I talk to about enrolment or fees?
faqs.a: For anything account-specific — your enrolment status, fees owed, or results — please contact Student Services directly or log in to my Student Centre, since I don't have access to individual student accounts.

faqs.q: I'm having a personal or safety concern, what do I do?
faqs.a: Please reach out to Federation's Respect and Safety service directly, or in an emergency call 1800 333 864. I can flag this for a real person to follow up, but safety concerns need direct human support.
